segments: 16. 'Go out,
and inform your people,
and flee, all of you,
because Salih is prepared to slaughter the Christians
and flee to Egypt.'
And everyone who was able arose and fled to Erbil
during the very days of Pentecost.
And in the morning of the day, when the slaves arose
and did not find Bar Yunis,
they supposed that he had preceded them to Mosul.
And they entered Mosul and informed Salih of the matter.
Then Salih was greatly afraid
lest Bar Yunis should reach the Tatars
and bring an army and seize him.
And he arose, took his son 'Ala al-Mulk and his slaves, and fled to Syria
in the month of Iyyar of this year.
And on the way, some of his slaves divided against him,
and they abandoned him and returned to Mosul,
and 'Alam Sanjar became their leader.
And when they came to enter Mosul,
the Mosulites, along with Yasan, the Mongol resident governor (shahnah), and Turkan Khatun the Khwarazmian, who had not consented to go with him, shut the gates against those who arrived.
And they remained for a few days besieging it.
Then a certain man whose name was Muhi bar Ziballaq—
the people of the Chaharsu, that is, the Four Markets that are in Mosul, joined him—
and they opened the gate of the city to him.
And 'Alam Sanjar and those with him entered.
Yasan fled with his companions,
while Turkan fortified herself in the citadel.
And when these entered Mosul,
they raised a great persecution against the Christians,
and plundered their houses,
and killed everyone who did not convert to Islam.
And many of the priests, deacons, notables, and common people denied their faith,
except for a few, namely, those of the house of Suwayd, and of Kuki, and Nafis the metalworker.
And outside, moreover, in the region of Nineveh,
as soon as King Salih fled,
the Kurds came down
and wrought a great slaughter among the Christians.
And they captured the Convent of the Sisters in Beth Kudida,
and slaughtered a great multitude of people in it,
who were hiding there from the whole region.
And moreover, those accursed ones went up to the Monastery of Mar Mattai,
and thousands of horsemen and foot soldiers gathered against it,
and they were fighting with the monks for a space of four months.
And they set up ladders
and wanted to scale the wall.
